speaker: Raj
text: Which brings us to tenth grade. Look at me. What chance do I have if I don't try too hard?

speaker: Penny
text: Howard, do you think maybe sometimes you try too hard? Well, you have a terrific chance. I mean, you're smart, you're funny, you have a cool job, you build stuff that goes into outer space.

speaker: Penny
text: No, look, I'm telling you, I've known you for like a year and a half, and this is the first time I feel like I'm talking to a real person. And you know what? I like him. He's a nice guy.

speaker: Raj
text: You really think so? I don't know.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Nice little bot you've got here. What's this do, spin?

speaker: Leonard
text: I'm aware. Yep. At 3400 RPM, it can cut through steel like it was wubber. Neat. Good work. Son, we've gotta call this off.

speaker: Sheldon
text: No, Leonard. For years, merciless thugs like Kripke have made my life a series of painful noogies and humiliating wedgies and the insensitively named Indian burns. Well, that stops now.

speaker: Raj
text: But, Sheldon, we don't have a chance. The only improvement you're able to make on the robot was to put fresh batteries in the remote.

speaker: Sheldon
text: What you fail to realize is Kripke suffers from a fatal flaw. Overconfidence from his robot's massive size and its overwhelming power.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Trust me, Kripke will fall easy prey to my psychological warfare. Observe. Kripke!

speaker: Sheldon
text: I would ask if your robot is prepared to meet its maker, but as you are its maker, clearly the two of you have met.
